rows.question: When I call requests.get(url), which function does the real work, and what does it do with the Session it creates?

rows.question: What happens when two cookies with the same name exist for different domains and I read one by name?
rows.answer: When you read a cookie by name without specifying a domain, the behavior depends on which method you use. The dict-style __getitem__ and get() both call _find_no_duplicates, which raises a CookieConflictError if more than one cookie matches the given name (and optional domain/path), so two cookies with the same name for different domains will trigger that error (src/requests/cookies.py:423-455, src/requests/cookies.py:191-227). Internally, Requests uses _find, which does not raise on conflicts but instead arbitrarily returns the value of the first matching cookie it encounters while iterating the jar (src/requests/cookies.py:401-421). To avoid the conflict, pass the domain (and optionally path) arguments to get() or use _find, which narrows the match to a single cookie (src/requests/cookies.py:191-227, src/requests/cookies.py:401-421).

rows.question: How do I delay downloading the response body until I want it?
rows.answer: Set the stream parameter to True when making the request so only the response headers are downloaded and the body is deferred until you access Response.content (docs/user/advanced.rst:300-329). You can then retrieve the body conditionally, e.g. if int(r.headers['content-length']) < TOO_LONG: content = r.content (docs/user/advanced.rst:300-329). rows.question: Does requests keep connections alive, and how do I turn that off?
